questions.question: When a car is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to create more space in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to create more space in front of you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, ride in a way that encourages them to pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the edge of the road mean?

options.text: The right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: How can you reduce your risk of a crash?

options.text: Hide your intentions from other drivers.
Stay very close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals and brake light. Stay in a good lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road in front, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you ride in the lane?

options.text: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This is usually the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors, so this position makes them more likely to see you.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Look for ways to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay back from the vehicle ahead, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or if another vehicle comes too fast from behind.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, what should you do before riding?

options.text: Decide if you can still ride based on how you feel.
Set a drinking limit so you can still ride safely.
Don't worry if you feel fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't ride.
questions.explanation: The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any alcohol. Even small amounts of alcohol can harm your ability to ride.

questions.question: What is a good way to deal with a tailgater?

options.text: Slow down or change lanes to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down or change lanes to let them pass.
questions.explanation: If it is safe, change lanes or slow down to let the tailgater pass. Speeding up will only make them continue to tailgate you at a higher speed, increasing danger.

questions.question: Compared to driving a car, riding a motorcycle is ______.
questions.correctAnswerText: More tiring
questions.explanation: Riding a motorcycle is more tiring than driving a car, especially on long trips. Do not ride when you are tired. Fatigue affects your ability to control the motorcycle.

questions.question: What fabric gives the most protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the best protection when riding.

questions.question: What should you think about when choosing where to ride in your lane?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
Which position makes your trip shorter.
Whether you can pass more vehicles from that position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that makes other drivers see you and gives you enough space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips. These are trips less than five miles long, often within the first few minutes of riding.

questions.question: If you think stopping your motorcycle will take longer than usual, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance on slippery surfaces. If your motorcycle needs more time to stop, stay farther away from the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: One benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance is that:

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks will take a lot of time.
Maintenance checks can help prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle will continue to run well if you maintain it regularly. Regular maintenance should be part of your routine care.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Help you blend in with traffic.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you an escape route.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: If your footwear has laces, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Tuck them in securely.
questions.explanation: Tuck in your shoelaces so they do not get caught on your motorcycle while riding.

questions.question: You can reduce serious injury in a crash by wearing:
questions.correctAnswerText: Face or eye protection.
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection in a crash. A plastic face shield helps protect your face from injury.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided red sign means you must stop.

questions.question: Smoothly downshifting on your motorcycle:

options.text: Allows you to use engine braking.
Should not be done around other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to use engine braking.
questions.explanation: Engine braking through smooth downshifting can help you slow down. If you use engine braking, turn on your brake lights separately so other drivers know you are slowing.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Exit their blind spot as fast as possible.
Slow down in the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit their blind spot as fast as possible.
questions.explanation: Get out of another vehicle's blind spot quickly. Move into the passing lane and speed up to pass the vehicle.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your regular scanning routine.
Do not help since you cannot change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of normal riding. Always check mirrors before changing lanes, stopping at an intersection, or slowing down.

questions.question: Besides watching for bad road conditions, riders should also look for:

options.text: Oncoming traffic that might turn left in front of you.
Traffic entering from side roads on the left and right.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Riders should constantly look ahead, to the sides, and behind their motorcycle. Watch for both bad road conditions and traffic that could be dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are about to combine into one lane.

questions.question: Which color is best to wear to be more visible?
questions.correctAnswerText: Orange
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green when riding. These colors make you easier to see at any time of day.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you may need to adjust:
questions.correctAnswerText: The suspension.
questions.explanation: Add a few pounds of pressure to your tires when carrying a passenger. Also adjust the suspension to handle the extra weight.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
Have only one set of footrests.
Not require the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat large enough for two riders. It should also have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear that you wear.

questions.question: The best source of information about your motorcycle is:

options.text: Someone who has a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: A simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see is to:

options.text: Ride with a large flag attached to its frame.
Ride with the headlight turned on.
Ride on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with the headlight turned on.
questions.explanation: Ride with your headlight on at all times. Also wear bright, reflective clothing and use your turn signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: Riding in the left third of the lane lets a driver see you in their side mirror. What is a problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
Wind may prevent drivers from using their side mirrors.
Drivers should not use their side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane where the driver is more likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of an accident, you should:

options.text: Try to blend into traffic and not be noticed.
Only use turn signals at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Ride very close to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: Be visible to other drivers by using turn signals, brake light, and proper lane position. Keep enough distance between you and other vehicles. Look 12 seconds ahead on the road and be ready to react to any danger.

questions.question: You should not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may need the lane.
It is hard to see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, if a hazard appears, that vehicle could block your escape path.
